Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center. EDSA Quezon Avenue. west Triangle. Quezon City http: //www. dilg.gov.ph OILG OPINION NO. S. 20 18 VICE-GOVERNOR VIRGINIA ALMONTE Office of the Vice-Governor Capitol, Oroquieta City Misamis Occidental Dear Vice-Governor Almonte: 22 AUG This has reference to your letter dated 22 September 2017 requesting for this Department's clarification on the following queries: I. Can Sangguniang Panlalawigan (SP) member Luansing's application for sick leave be approved considering that she has not yet returned back to work (leaves were submitted by her staff on her behalf) and in the absence of a medical certificate? 2. Can the request of SP member Luansing to file for one year leave of absence without pay to take care of legal issues being raised against their family be accommodated? 3. What is the DILG's position on the sick leave applications of elective officials? At what point are they required to submit medical certificate (since they only file leaves on session dates)? Would this translate to more than five (5) consecutive session dates that she has been absent? While it is true that Sanggunian is required to hold session once a week or four (4) times a month, this does not mean that their duties and responsibilities is limited and confined to attending sessions. Please be guided that this Department has settled in its previous legal opinions that an elective official is deemed in the service of their constituents regardless of time and place. Thus, they are given wide latitude of discretion on how to effectively run their respective LGUs. They may not be present at their respective offices but this does not mean that they are automatically absent from work. To bolster this, the Supreme Court in the case of Macatangay vs. Chairman of Commission on Auditi has ruled that: ' G.R. No. L-38728, 30 September 1982 11 Page

"In fact, they are not even required to keep a record of their daily attendance such as by accomplishing Civil Service Form No. 48 (Daily Time Record) or punching the bundy clock. xxv Elective officials, indeed, are deemed in the service of their constituents regardless of time and place. There can be no occasion to consider them absent from work since their presence at such specified time and place is not a pre-requisite to their collection of salary for services rendered. " It is further emphasize in DILG Legal Opinion No. 23, S.2005, where this Department has opined that: 'lxxx Section 81, 3d par. of the Local Government Code of 1991 provides that Elective local officials shall be entitled to the same privileges as those enjoyed by appointive local officials, including the commulation and commutation thereof Corollary thereto, Section 5 of Civil Service Commission (CSC) Memorandum Circular No. 41, S. 1998 also provides that local elective officials shall be entitled to leaveprivileges as those enjoyed by appointive elocal officials. In this regard, Section 57 ofthe above-mentioned circular alsoprovides that leave without pay not exceeding one year may be granted, in addition to the vacation and/or sick leave earned. Leave without pay in excess done month shall require the clearance of the proper head of department or agency. Ergo, we are of the VI?w that a leave of absence for one year may be availed of by the concerned Punong Barangay'! (Underscoring supplied) It is clear from the above-given opinion that leave of absence for one year may be availed of by an elective official provided that he/she shall secure clearance from the Vice- Governor pursuant to Section 47 of the LGC and Article 84 of its Implementing Rules and Regulations2. Moreover, in CSC Resolution No. 001495 dated 26 June 2000, re: 'BARANGA Y OFFICIALS; LEA VE PRIVILEGES; MATERNITY BENEFITS", it was resolved that: 'Based on the afore-quoted provisions of law, it is clear that local elective and appointive officials are entitled to leave privileges 2 DILG Opinion No. 27, S. 2009, dated 27 May2009 21 Page

provided under Article 172, Rule AXII, Rules and Regulations Implementing the Local Government Code of 1991. These include: "(b) Sick leave — Officials and employees of an LGU shall also be entitled to fifteen (15) days sick leave with full pay for each year of service. Such leave shall be computed exclusive of Saturdays, Sundays, and Holidays. It should, however, be stiBsed that the grant of the abovesaid is subject to the standards set by the Civil Service Commission (CSC), including cumulation and commutation thereof (Article 172, Rule MV, Rules and Regulations Implementing the Local Government Code of 1991; Article 77, supra). Moreover, local elective offcials are entitled to leave privileges effective May 12, 1983 pursuant to Batas Pambansa 337 and Local Government Cde of1991. (CSCMCNo. u, series of1999). Be that as it may, it is recommended that your concern be submitted to the Civil Service Commission, as the subject matter herein, leave of officials, pertains to their mandate and technical expertise . Further, Section 78 of the LGC declares that: "SEC. 78. All matters pertin ent to h uman resources and development in the local government units shall be governed by the civil service laws and such rules and regulations and other issuances promulgated pursuant thereto, unless otherwise specified in this Code. " We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Very truly yours, By Auth Of the Secretary: ERO CC: Dir. Arnel M. Agabe Regional Director DILG-Region X Undersecretary 3 IP age
